input.quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term. Vendor warrants it has authority to enter the Agreement and grant the rights stated here.
input.rationale: Compliant at the preferred position; no redline and no counterparty comment required. Duration: the deterministic period check is a false negative because the period is spelled out in words rather than digits — "ninety days" in Section 19.2 is 90 days, meeting the >=90-day benchmark, and it runs from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, so it is in substance longer than 90 days from delivery. Hosted Services must conform "throughout the subscription term" (the full term under Section 8.1), exceeding the preferred 12-month software period. Substance: 19.1 warrants professional and workmanlike performance by qualified personnel in accordance with industry standards, the Agreement and each Order Form, plus material conformance of Services and Deliverables to documentation and agreed specifications; 19.3 adds a no-malicious-code warranty and Applicable Law compliance, together with no functionality diminution and open-source protection. Remedy: 19.4 requires prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge and, if that fails within a reasonable period, termination of the affected item with a refund of Fees paid, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims — matching the preferred repair/replace/refund remedy. Disclaimer: 19.5 is mutual, confined to implied warranties, and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity, confidentiality or data-protection duty, or stated remedy, so it cannot swallow the express warranties and there is no "AS IS" walk-away risk. Minor sub-element noted only, not flagged: the 19.3 malicious-code warranty covers code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" rather than all malicious code, which is a sub-element short of the ideal wording and is mitigated by the security obligations in Section 17; we would accept it rather than reopen Section 19. Retained as internal evidence.
